Private Henry "Black Death" Johnson, a recent recipient of the American Medal of Honor, wearing his Croix de Guerre medal. France. 1918

While on guard duty on May 14, 1918, Private Johnson came under attack by a large German raider party which may have numbered as many as 24 German soldiers. Johnson used his rifle, a bolo knife and his bare fists to repel the Germans and rescued a comrade from capture. Johnson suffered 21 wounds during this ordeal. This earned him the nickname of "Black Death" from his comrades.

Despite his wounds, he was denied a military disability pension and died penniless in a veterans hospital in 1929. He was the first American to receive the French Croix de Guerre with special citation and a golden palm; their highest award for bravery. His home country eventually awarded him a Purple Heart in 1996, the Distinguished Service Cross in 2003 and, finally,their highest honor, the Medal of Honor on June 2, 2015.
